Tom — adding the technical sketch from our side so you have concrete numbers ahead of the probe. This is a conservative profile; we can tighten after we see your traces.

Summary (assumptions: 1 active streaming connection = 1 concurrent session; average token generation CPU path):
- Baseline sizing: 200 aggregate QPS -> expect ~60 concurrent sessions for streaming (avg session = 3–4 tokens/s).
- Burst handling: We recommend capacity headroom for 3x sustained bursts. With your 600 QPS short spikes, we advise either short-term capacity burst on Dedicated or using Redwood’s autoscale policy with burst queueing (est. 90–120ms extra tail latency when queueing).

Latency matrix (provisional):
- Local-region peering (Helios VPC -> Redwood Private same cloud region):
  - p50: 40–60ms
  - p95: 90–130ms
  - p99: 180–260ms (target: keep <=250ms for SLO)
- Cross-region fallback (peering interrupted, route to hosted region):
  - p50: 80–120ms
  - p95: 160–230ms
  - p99: 300–420ms (recommend SLO of 400ms max)

Concurrency guidance:
- Streaming (long-lived connections): prioritize keeping session alive (MTU and NAT keepalive important). Recommend NAT timeout >= 300s or configure TCP keepalive every 60s.
- Polling (short-lived): higher per-request overhead — expect additional 40–80ms overhead versus streaming for auth handshake and TLS.

Egress considerations:
- We will provide a short cost-sensitivity doc — egress is metered on the peering path vs hosted; if you route to the hosted fallback, egress will pass through Redwood's region billing.

Operational fallback behavior (what Redwood will do):
- If peering latency exceeds a configurable threshold for 10s, requests are routed to the next-available region or degraded model variant. We can set your fallbacks to (1) degrade model size, (2) change to polling mode, or (3) redirect to hosted region — pick order.

Next deliverables we will send today:
- Updated SLO matrix (in sheet) with concrete QPS/concurrency rows.
- Probe script and minimal instructions.

Attaching the SLO matrix export and the sample capture template you can pass to your infra team.

—Aditya
